name: shake-vertical
concept: A vertical version of the classic shake: a quick up-down rattle that runs once and returns to rest. Use it when the wrong element is a row, a field, or anything better judged by vertical motion than horizontal.

name: shake-diagonal
concept: A one-shot rattle that moves along a diagonal instead of a single axis. Use it to signal an error without matching the plain horizontal shake already used elsewhere on the page.

name: jolt
concept: One sharp sideways displacement and an immediate return to rest. The plainest way to say a single hard impact happened, once, with nothing left oscillating.

name: jolt-down
concept: A single sharp downward displacement that snaps back to rest. Use it for a drop, a sudden weight, or an item that just landed hard.

name: jolt-up
concept: A single sharp upward displacement that snaps back to rest. Use it for a sudden push, a jump-scare beat, or a quick recoil away from something.

name: rattle-snap
concept: A single overshoot-and-settle motion: the element snaps out, rebounds past center, then eases to rest. Use it for a toggle, a chip, or anything that should feel elastic when it corrects itself.

name: judder
concept: A rapid vertical judder that decays across the cycle before coming to rest, like a jolt working itself out. Use it for turbulence, a rough landing, or a glitchy correction.

name: tremor-burst
concept: A brief multi-directional tremor that decays quickly and stops. Use it for a small system hiccup or a momentary loss of stability that resolves on its own.

name: shudder
concept: A single full-body shudder combining a small rotation with a sideways rattle, decaying to rest. Use it for revulsion, cold, or a strong one-time reaction.

name: recoil
concept: A quick pull backward followed by a small forward overshoot before settling, like recoil from a kick. Use it for a fired action, a strong click, or a triggered event.

name: flinch
concept: A very quick, very small upward flinch and recovery. Use it for a light, momentary reaction to something unexpected but minor.

name: stagger-step
concept: An uneven, asymmetric sequence of horizontal steps that reads as staggering off balance before it settles. Use it for a loss of footing or an off-balance correction.

name: rattle-double
concept: Two short rattle bursts in a row, separated by a brief pause, then rest. Use it when one shake isn't emphatic enough and the error deserves a second reminder.

name: shake-fade
concept: A shake whose amplitude grows across the cycle, peaks, then snaps back to rest, instead of staying constant. Use it for tension that escalates toward a single release, like a countdown reaching zero.

name: quake-jolt
concept: A single strong diagonal displacement with a small rebound before resting, larger and rougher than the plain jolt. Use it for a heavier one-time impact, like a nearby explosion or a hard collision.

name: buzz-off
concept: A single fast burst of tiny horizontal vibration, like one phone buzz, then stillness. Use it for a one-time notification tap rather than an ongoing alert.

name: knock
concept: A single brief downward dip, like a knuckle knocking once, then rest. Use it for a light tap acknowledgment rather than an error.

name: twitch
concept: One small, quick rotational twitch and back, over almost before it registers. Use it for a subtle single reflex, like an eye twitch or a brief glitch.

name: rattle-rotate
concept: A one-shot rattle built from rotation instead of translation, swinging back and forth before settling flat. Use it for a hinge, a lever, or anything that should visibly pivot when it errors.

name: shiver-burst
concept: A brief, fast, tiny multi-directional shiver that runs once, like a single cold shudder. Use it for a momentary chill or a quick uneasy reaction.

name: vibrate-fine
concept: A very small amplitude, very fast, continuous horizontal vibration. Use it for something actively buzzing right now, like a ringing phone icon or a live alert badge.

name: vibrate-buzz
concept: A continuous small two-axis buzz, slightly larger and less linear than a fine vibrate. Use it for a device that is actively humming or vibrating in the user's hand.

name: tremor-slow
concept: A slow, continuous, larger-amplitude tremor that never fully settles. Use it to build dread before something happens, like a monster approaching or a structure about to fail.

name: tremor-deep
concept: An even slower and larger continuous tremor than tremor-slow, for the deepest sense of dread. Use it for a large structure, a giant footstep, or an approaching catastrophe.

name: rattle-loop
concept: A continuous rotational rattle at a moderate pace, swinging left and right around center. Use it for an ongoing mechanical fault, a loose hinge, or a warning that keeps pivoting for attention.

name: rattle-tilt
concept: A fast, small, continuous rotational flutter, quicker and tighter than rattle-loop. Use it for a small icon that needs a nervous, persistent tilt.

name: shake-two-axis
concept: A continuous shake where the horizontal and vertical motion peak at different points in the cycle, so the two axes feel slightly out of phase. Use it for a richer, more organic ongoing shake than a single-axis loop.

name: shake-orbit
concept: A continuous shake that traces a small square-ish loop path around center rather than a straight back-and-forth line. Use it for a distinctive, ongoing agitation that reads differently from a linear shake.

name: tremble-vertical
concept: A continuous, moderate-speed vertical tremble, smaller and gentler than a judder. Use it for a persistently nervous or unstable element that never fully resolves.

name: tremble-horizontal
concept: A continuous, moderate-speed horizontal tremble, distinct in rhythm and amplitude from the finer vibrate loops. Use it for a persistently nervous element that shakes side to side rather than up and down.

name: nervous-jitter
concept: A continuous, irregular multi-axis jitter with uneven timing between moves, reading as erratic rather than mechanical. Use it for anxiety, nervousness, or an unstable connection.

name: alert-vibrate
concept: A continuous small combined rotation and shift, the rhythm of a notification badge that keeps nudging for attention. Use it for an unread count or an alert icon that should feel urgent but not chaotic.

name: earthquake
concept: A rough, continuous, multi-axis shake with irregular amplitude and a slight rotation, reading as chaotic and uncontrolled. Use it for a large-scale disaster or a system in genuine crisis.

name: rumble
concept: A continuous, low, mostly vertical rumble with a dense, textured rhythm rather than a clean oscillation. Use it for an engine, distant thunder, or heavy machinery running nearby.

name: chatter
concept: A very fast, tiny, continuous vertical chatter, reading like teeth chattering from cold or fear. Use it for a small icon that needs a rapid, high-frequency nervous energy.

name: flutter-shake
concept: A continuous small vertical bob paired with an alternating rotation, giving a light fluttering shake rather than a rigid one. Use it for something delicate that is nonetheless agitated, like a moth near a flame.

name: dread-tremor
concept: A continuous loop that stays nearly still for most of the cycle, then erupts into a sudden burst of motion before settling again. Use it for a slow-burn sense of dread punctuated by sudden unease.

name: crescendo-shake
concept: A continuous shake whose amplitude ramps up from nearly nothing to a strong displacement each cycle, then resets and builds again. Use it for a repeating countdown, a charging attack, or mounting tension that keeps recurring.

name: simmer-shake
concept: A continuous, very subtle diagonal shake, small enough to read as simmering tension rather than an active alarm. Use it for a background state that is quietly unstable without demanding attention.

name: rattle-cage
concept: A continuous combined rotation and horizontal rattle with larger amplitude, like something pushing against a latched door. Use it for a contained threat straining against its container.

name: panic-vibrate
concept: A continuous, very fast diagonal vibration with irregular, varying amplitude at each step, reading as frantic rather than steady. Use it for a critical alarm or a system that has lost control.

name: static-buzz
concept: An ultra-fine, ultra-fast continuous vibration paired with a faint opacity flicker, like static electricity crackling. Use it for a broken connection, a glitching display, or electrical interference.

name: jitter-diagonal
concept: A continuous fast diagonal jitter alternating between two opposite corners. Use it for a small element that needs a persistent, slightly aggressive nervous energy.

name: quiver
concept: A continuous, soft vertical quiver with a slight rotation, gentler and slower than a chatter. Use it for a delicate, timid motion rather than an urgent one.

name: teeter-rattle
concept: A slow, continuous, larger-angle rotational teeter, like something balanced precariously about to tip. Use it for instability or imbalance rather than urgency.

name: rattle-fast
concept: A very fast, small, continuous rotational rattle, quicker than both rattle-loop and rattle-tilt. Use it for a small part that is spinning loose or vibrating at high frequency.

name: alert-ring-shake
phrase: shake with an expanding alert ring
concept: A continuous small shake paired with an expanding, fading ring of shadow around the element, like a radar ping crossed with a warning rattle. This is the library's one shake-family entry that also uses a box-shadow ring; use it for a critical, location-pinned alert.

name: tremor-diagonal
concept: A slow, continuous diagonal tremor, distinct in rhythm and amplitude from both the straight tremor-slow and the fast jitter-diagonal. Use it for an ongoing unease that reads along a single diagonal line.

name: vibrate-hum
concept: A continuous small vibration paired with a subtle brightness pulse, like a device humming and warming up as it runs. Use it for active machinery or an energized element that should feel alive.

name: shudder-cold
concept: A continuous, fast, small multi-axis shudder, colder and more chaotic than the gentler simmer-shake. Use it for an ongoing chill or a persistent state of being unsettled.
